summary: Bug fix VERIFIED: MS_CLIENT_SECRET now accepted by Microsoft (Azure AD). Callback with a fake code + valid state returns AADSTS9002313 ('invalid_grant') instead of the previous AADSTS7000215 ('invalid_client' / 'Invalid client secret provided'). This proves Microsoft is authenticating our client credentials successfully and rejecting only the authorization code. All 14 regression tests from iteration_1 also pass.

bug_fix_verification.bug: AADSTS7000215 Invalid client secret provided (Secret ID vs Value confusion)

microsoft_response.error_description: AADSTS9002313: Invalid request. Request is malformed or invalid.

evidence.old_expected_error_absent: AADSTS7000215 / invalid_client NOT present in response

passed: GET /api/auth/microsoft/url returns valid URL with state persisted in oauth_states
critical_code_review_comments: Consider narrowing OAuth `scope` at token endpoint call — Microsoft docs recommend omitting `offline_access User.Read` on token exchange when scopes are already granted in the /authorize step; harmless but unusual.
oauth_states collection has no TTL index; abandoned states accumulate. Add a TTL index on `created_at` (e.g., 10 min) to auto-clean.
Sessions never expire and refresh_token failures don't invalidate the session doc; consider setting session TTL or clearing on refresh failure.
server.py is a single 460-line file; when adding features consider splitting auth / onedrive / maps into modules.
seed_data_creation: Tests inject a temporary TEST_ prefixed session + map in MongoDB and clean them up in teardown_class. oauth_states are auto-cleaned by the callback endpoint or explicitly deleted in tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: MS OAuth client secret bug (AADSTS7000215) is verified as FIXED. Real OAuth code exchange still requires a browser-driven flow which cannot be tested backend-only. Graph-calling endpoints (/onedrive/files, /onedrive/files/{id}/sheets, /maps/{id}/data) require a real MS access token so they remain untested. Use /app/backend/tests/test_ms_oauth_callback.py as the regression baseline.
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: MS_CLIENT_SECRET in backend/.env contained the Azure AD 'Secret ID' (a GUID) instead of the actual secret 'Value'. Azure returned AADSTS7000215 on token exchange. Fix: replaced with the actual client-secret value 'tVM8Q~~emDBjMM-585d.dAvXGmnTUINqdUmXKb~U'. Verification: sending a fake authorization code but a valid registered state now yields invalid_grant/AADSTS9002313 from Microsoft instead of invalid_client, confirming client credentials are accepted.
